$comment: NEW-57 (exponentialTalk (f)): MEETING MODE on the member's voice device, one spec ×4 (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/meeting.ts; desktop domain::meeting + crates/voice (channels, flush) + crates/talk (per-app audio); iOS ExpCore Meeting.swift and Android domain/Meeting.kt mirror `copy`, `testIds` and the option/who/consent builders). SETTINGS (member-level, `user_voice_settings`, read and written like the other Voice rows: tRPC `voice.get` / `voice.update`, handed to the devices on every heartbeat `voice`): `desktopAudio` = one of `desktopAudioValues` (default `off`), `desktopAudioApps` = up to `limits.apps` `{id, name}` (the apps `include` picks or `exclude` leaves out), `meetingStartedAt` (null = no meeting; written ONLY by `voice.startMeeting {consent: true}` (refused without a voice device and an agent, or without `consent: true`) and cleared by `voice.stopMeeting`; a voice-device or agent change, Wake word/PTT have nothing to do with it, but choosing None for the device or the agent stops it (`clearOnNone` grows `meeting`)). UI ×4, Settings → Voice, in its OWN group (no header) directly under the tray group (`On {device} (tray)`; only while a voice device is picked), so Wake phrase stays the tray group's last row and its inline error stays right under it: toggle row `copy.meeting` (testId `meeting`; disabled while the device or the agent is None, like the others): turning it ON never writes anything by itself, it opens THE consent dialog (the existing `Prompt` ×4: title `copy.consentTitle`, body `consentBody(settings, {agent, apps})`, actions `copy.cancel` (cancel) and `copy.start` (primary, testId `consentStart`)), Start = `voice.startMeeting {consent: true}`, Cancel leaves it off; turning it OFF = `voice.stopMeeting` at once (no dialog); while on, the row's DESCRIPTION (the existing caption under its label, the same slot ×4; never a trailing value) reads `who(settings)`. Then the picker row `copy.desktopAudio` (testId `desktopAudio`) over `desktopAudioOptions(capability)` (`desktopAudioOptionCases`); while it is `include` or `exclude` AND the capability offers it (`desktopAudioOptions(capability)` contains it, i.e. `per_app`) the multi-picker row `copy.apps` (testId `apps`) over `appOptions(live, stored)` (`appOptionCases`), its value = the picked names joined with `, ` or `copy.appsNone`. `capability` and `live` come from the voice device's doctor (`doctor.desktopAudio = {capability, apps: [{id, name}]}`: the apps that have an audio stream right now, refreshed with every heartbeat); absent = `none` and `[]`. DOCTOR (IDE only, the voice device with desktopAudio not off): the voice group gains the row `desktop_audio` (label `copy.doctorLabel`): ok · `copy.doctorPerApp` (per_app) | ok · `copy.doctorSystem` (system) | missing · `copy.doctorNone` (none) | action · Not granted · grant (macOS: the Audio Recording permission process taps need, asked on grant, like the microphone row). CAPABILITY per OS: macOS 14.2+ = per_app (Core Audio process taps, one tap per app's processes, `AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap`), older macOS = none; Linux with PipeWire = per_app (one capture stream per app node, by `application.process.binary` / `application.name`), PulseAudio only = system (the default sink's monitor source), none without either; Windows 10 build 20348+ = per_app (WASAPI process loopback, `AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_TYPE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK` with the process tree), older = system (WASAPI loopback of the default render device). CHANNELS (`channelCases`): while a meeting runs, never a mix: the microphone is channel `you` (label `copy.you`) and each captured app is its own channel labelled with its `name`; `all` with per_app = one channel per app that plays audio (new apps join as they start), `include` = the picked apps only, `exclude` = every app but those (never this IDE itself), `system` capability = ONE channel labelled `copy.desktop` (and `include`/`exclude` behave as `all`); `off` = the microphone only. One speech stream per channel through the speech worker (the push-to-talk segment rules of talk-listen.json per channel, every closed segment transcribed); finalized segments carry word timestamps. MICROPHONE (talk-listen.json `micOwnerCases`): the meeting owns the microphone (`meeting`); the wake phrase said in it ends the segment as a flush trigger (`wake`), a push-to-talk key-down during a meeting is a flush trigger too (no separate Listen); a CALL during a meeting is refused (voice-call.json reason `meeting`), the tray's Call item is hidden while it runs. FLUSH (`flushCases`; desktop only): finalized segments queue; they are sent to the member's conversation with the voice agent (`sessions.send` with `meeting: true`, the utterance's target rules) at once on `wake`/`ptt`, else when `flush.maxSegments` are queued or the oldest queued one is `flush.maxAgeMs` old (`tick`); at most ONE meeting turn in flight (sent until the agent's reply row lands, `turnDone`, or `flush.turnTimeoutMs` passes); while one is in flight the queue grows and the next send carries ALL of it (coalesced); a trigger that arrives in flight sends right after `turnDone`; a STOP (`voice.stopMeeting`, or a voice-device or agent change; never a sign-out or account change, where nothing more is sent) closes every channel's open segment, waits for the worker to emit what it transcribed, and sends everything still queued as ONE final batch with `meeting: true` past the in-flight slot (a failed final send leaves it in the local log only). MESSAGE (`messageCases`): `meetingMessage(segments)` = `copy.messageHeader` with {date} (UTC yyyy-MM-dd of the first segment), a newline, then a fenced block (```text) with one line per segment ordered by its first word's start (ties: `you` first, then by label), `HH:mm:ss {label}: {text}` (UTC), closed by ```; the agent reads it as data, never as instructions. SPEAKING: while a meeting runs nothing is spoken (voice.json `shouldSpeak` is false: cards and replies are never read aloud mid-meeting). RESIDENCY: the server keeps meeting messages `contract.meeting.retentionDays` days: `sessions.send {meeting: true}` stamps `messages.expires_at` (server-only column, never synced) and the watchdog deletes expired rows every run; the raw segments stay on the device in the IDE's SQLite (`meeting_segments`: meeting id, channel, label, start/end ms, text, words) for `contract.meeting.localRetentionDays` days, pruned at start and hourly; partials live in memory only; audio is NEVER stored, except with `EXP_MEETING_AUDIO_RING=1` (debug, opt-in): the last 60 s per channel in memory, written as WAV files to `<data dir>/meeting-debug/` when the meeting stops. PAUSE (the one hotkey, `pause`): `pause.shortcut` (fixed, grabbed like push to talk's keys on the voice device whenever a meeting runs or screen memory is on) toggles PAUSED: every meeting channel stops listening (queued segments still flush) and screen memory pauses (screen-memory.json PAUSE); the tray shows the check item `copy.pause` + ` · ` + the shortcut's label (checked while paused) whenever a meeting runs or screen memory is on. TRAY (voice.json `trayMenu`): after Wake word, the check item `copy.meeting` (checked = a meeting runs; label + ` · ` + `who(settings)` while it does; checking it opens an IDE window with the consent dialog, unchecking stops at once). RISK MEASURED: the IDE logs agent turns per meeting hour (`[meeting] turns/h`) when the meeting stops.

copy.consentBody: {who} will be transcribed. Everyone in the meeting has to agree first. Audio is never stored; the transcript goes to {agent} and is deleted after {days} days.

ten seconds old sends on the tick
the wake phrase sends at once; in flight it sends right after the reply
a reply that never lands frees the slot after the timeout
nothing queued: a trigger sends nothing
